precepts.text: Zacharias and Elisabeth walked in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless: human beings can keep God's laws.
precepts.point: The scripture also says we are gods but shall die like men, so we are the two anyway; for not keeping the commandments we die like men.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
Christ said to men, “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” The trinity doctrine says no: only God can keep the commandments, so Christ cannot be fully a man, because a full man can't keep those laws, but a full man and a full God can. The insidiousness behind it is to make it impossible for man to keep God's commandments.

Luke answers that with John the Baptist's parents, Zacharias and Elisabeth: “And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” Both righteous. Walking in all the commandments. Blameless: that's perfect. So human beings can keep God's commandments, perfect as the Father in heaven. It can be done.

The scripture also says we are gods but shall die like men, so we are the two anyway; for not keeping the commandments we die like men.

Peel back the layers of confusion and the doctrine is all about removing the humanity of Christ, or keeping some of it and making him a god too, so that man can't keep the commandments: Christ kept the laws so we don't have to do anything. That's the whole premise behind the great swelling words. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments. Where is Christmas, New Year, Halloween, carnival, Labor Day, the Fourth of July or birthdays in the Bible? Your three-in-one God has nothing to say about them.

precepts.text: Let your yeas be yea, and your nays be nay, and everything else is what? Everything else is evil.
precepts.point: Hey, Malachi, how many times you hear, brother, listen, brother, stop talking. Brother, stop talking. Oh, God. Brother, I'm trying to help you. Stop talking. Oh my goodness. You don't realise. You think you saying something deep, you're burying yourself. He just can't stop talking. Let your yeas be yea, and your nays be nay, and everything else is what? Nobody knows the scripture. What is it? Everything else is evil. The scripture says in a multitude of words there lacketh not, or wanteth not, sin. It means does not lack. You're over-explaining. Why does she have your phone? Well, okay, there you go. This is your senses being exercised.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.” Wanteth not means it does not lack: where there are many words, sin is never missing. Christ gave the rule for our speech: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay, and everything else is evil.

How many times do you hear it: brother, listen, stop talking. Brother, I am trying to help you, stop talking. You think you are saying something deep, and you are burying yourself. He just cannot stop talking.

Take the brother at work who handed his phone to a girl while the other brother stepped to the back. Asked why, he said it was nothing. Then it was business. What business do you have with her, when we just walked into this place? Nah, it was nothing. Now you are repeating yourself. That is the multitude of words, the over-explaining, and it gave him away. Just by seeing the phone the other brother knew something was not right, and there was more behind it.

That is the ears and the eyes being exercised. Your ears have to be tuned to the subtleties in speech, and a man's face will tell you what is really going on, not what he says. The heart takes what it has seen and heard, processes it and comes to a conclusion; to discern between good and evil you have to be spiritual. Speech reveals the thoughts formed in the heart, so the one who refrains his lips and keeps his yea to yea and his nay to nay is wise.

precepts.text: The key is without a cause. Meaning if I'm mad with you and I have no reason to be mad with you, I'm in danger of judgment. But now somebody does something to your daughter, your wife, your loved one; do you have a reason? Yes. The dude said, in order to be a man of peace, you must be capable of great violence. If you're not capable of violence, you're just harmless.
precepts.point: I met this one brother years ago at camp Eastern Parkway. He's on medication. He said, I would join you, but I have psychosis; I can't work, I get violent. I said, why? He says, I hate white people. He said, when I sit in the office or if I'm doing construction, I'll look at them and I just want to harm them.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”. The key is without a cause. If I'm mad with you and I have no reason to be mad with you, I'm in danger of judgment.

But now somebody does something to your daughter, your wife, your loved one: do you have a reason? Yes. At one of the schools a sister's phone kept going ding, somebody sending her indecent pictures on Instagram. It went on for a while until the heads of the school had everybody bring their phones up and closed the doors. One brother said his phone was dead; they said don't worry, we got a charger. Sure enough, it was him. They told everybody to move back, and the husband said, move out my way. That is anger with a cause.

As the saying goes, in order to be a man of peace you must be capable of great violence; if you're not capable of violence, you're just harmless. So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” forbids hatred without a cause, not the defense of your own.

precepts.point: And such were some of you: everybody in here can identify with something on that list and say, I used to do that. But ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God. We are washed with the word of God.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“Be not deceived: neither fornicators”, “nor adulterers”. Fornication covers the whole list of sexual sins in Leviticus 18. And for the porno brothers, Christ said: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.”

So porn falls into that category. It is adultery in the heart, and adulterers shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

Who still struggles with porn? Not who is always watching; who still struggles with it? Nine hands went up in the room. The fight is real, and it has to be named for what it is before it can be fought.

precepts.text: Whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment; the name calling continues the sin, and whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire. That is when God has to step in.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
“Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”.

It does not start with the murder. It starts with anger at your brother without a cause. “and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council”. Raca means thou fool, vain fellow, and the council there is man’s council.

“but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.” Just continuing the sin, the name calling and all of that, puts you in danger of hell fire. That is when God has to step in.

These are the attributes of Simon, and the class is a self-examination for all of us. Simon’s anger toward Onias turned into slander and name calling, calling him a traitor, and it ended in murder.

precepts.text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
precepts.point: For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto. Blessed are the peacemakers, but peace does not always work with some people; some spirits are grimy, and at the end of the day they don't want peace with you.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Onias the high priest went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private.” He did not even go there to accuse Simon. That shows the character of Onias III, a great and upstanding elder man.

Christ says, “Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.” That is the attribute of Onias. His own people had turned on him, Simon had one of his priests murdered, and the governor was raging against him, and still he went seeking the good of all, public and private, not revenge.

That is what a child of God does. Simon’s spirit lusts, envies, slanders and kills to get the upper hand. The peacemaker seeks the good of the whole nation.

precepts.text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid? How do you fix it? You have to control what you view. You have to control what you desire. Seeing a beautiful woman does not mean you should think lustfully about her. Especially you married men: you should have a covenant with your eyes with your wife.
precepts.point: Pornography and private sin. Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. A lot of you brothers and sisters be doing that: scrolling until something catches your eye, then down the rabbit hole, not caring about any consequences, fully convinced and convicted in your sin.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
Matthew 5:28 says whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her “hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” A lot of you brothers do that, and a lot of you sisters do that. You're scrolling down, you see something that catches your eye, and next thing you know you are going down the rabbit hole, full-fledged, not caring about no consequences, fully convinced and convicted in your sin. How do you fix that? Job 31.

“I made a covenant with mine eyes”. You have to control what you view. You have to control what you desire. “why then should I think upon a maid?” I should not be thinking lustfully upon a maid. Because you see a beautiful woman doesn't mean you should think lustfully about that sister; you made a covenant with your eyes. Especially you married men: you should have a covenant with your eyes with your wife. Why should I even think about it?

“For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?” The one who looks to lust has already committed adultery in his heart, and what portion does he have from God then, what inheritance from the Almighty? Read on and Job answers: “Is not destruction to the wicked?”

That is how the private sin of pornography is fought: not after the eye has wandered, but by making the covenant beforehand, so that the looking that leads to adultery in the heart never begins.

precepts.text: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come. How is it going to be preached in all the world if you have no plans and no implementation to do anything worldwide? The Lord sent his prophets with vision and goals to take it to the ends of the earth.
precepts.point: Ye are the light of the world. The scriptures tell us this is a global mission, worldwide. We have to have our aspirations and goals set to a global standard, not a local one.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“Ye are the light of the world.” Not the light of Brooklyn, not the light of one city: of the world. When the Lord sent us out, he sent us out as a light to the whole world, and Matthew 24 shows how far that light has to go.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” How is it going to be preached in all of the world if you have no plans, no plan of action, no implementation to do anything worldwide? How are you the guys if you ain't got global goals and you ain't touching the ends of the earth?

The Lord sent his prophets with vision, with goals, with aspirations to take it to the ends of the earth. That is why leadership puts things in place: “Where there is no vision, the people perish.” This is a global mission, and our aspirations and goals have to be set to a global standard, not a local one.

So the light of the world is a people carrying the gospel of the kingdom to all nations, and the end does not come until that witness has gone out.

“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Our people are the remnant, scattered to the four corners of the world.

How are these people going to be able to rise out of these places if they were never told? That is why this gospel has to have a global standard, preached to the whole world. If your leadership ain't talking about covering the earth, they're not the guys. Don't waste your time.

They ridicule us now: y'all going over there to Africa, y'all in India, you went to Australia, you went to Papua New Guinea. We don't give a damn how anybody feels about it. Negro, you do lack the understanding of this Bible; you do err, not knowing the scriptures. The people have been scattered to the four corners. How are you going to reach them if your aspirations are just down the street, if you want to be known for Times Square or a street corner?

Where would we be today if this truth had stayed in Harlem, if it never left the streets of Brooklyn? Where a lot of these other camps are. Being the light of the world means going where the remnant was scattered, to the islands of the sea, and telling them who they are.

precepts.text: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: That would be many of our sons and daughters who refuse to listen to their parents. If it isn't jail, it's a pregnancy, a disease, a marriage riddled with alcohol abuse and domestic violence. The parents in righteousness are supposed to oversee who their sons and daughters get hooked up with. That's why God gave children parents.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
“For rulers are not a terror to good works”. The powers that be are not a terror to those of us that keep the commandments of God. Even though we are persecuted for it, it is not a terror to us, because we know what it is about. We are in captivity, but we are doing what God said to do, and they are going to have to answer to the Father for their mistreatment of us.

That is because of this promise: “Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” If I am going to get locked up for doing what is right, I will suffer for that.

Being persecuted for righteousness’ sake deals with a whole different kind of mentality. All the words they say to me will not mean anything, because I am suffering for a worthy cause, and I know that after that, mine is the kingdom of heaven. You can go through that trial and say, the Lord is going to receive me because I did what was right.

That is a totally different mentality than going in as a murderer. Suffering as a murderer, you are still going to get jacked up at the end; you are not getting the kingdom. So do that which is good, and if the rulers persecute you for it, the kingdom of heaven is yours.

precepts.text: Christ said, Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect. You see it right there in red.
precepts.point: The wondrous thing out of God's commandments: he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
Christ says it plainly: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” You see it right there in red. For those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence: this is Christ himself speaking.

That is the wondrous thing the psalmist asks to behold: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” When I keep God’s commandments, the wondrous thing I see out of them is that he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him, perfect as our Father in heaven is perfect.

Those eyes are not only the bodily eyes. They are the spiritual eyes, the insight to see this word and the situation we are in, and to understand that it is all spiritual. That is why we have to delve into the scriptures and meditate, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law, and after we understand and observe, apply it and be like our Father.

precepts.text: Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. That is exactly how lust is conceived: it starts with the look, and then the thought, in your heart, before anything physical ever happens.
precepts.point: And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death. Some of you say, I fornicated and I did not die. That death is talking about damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

precepts.why:
“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin.” Where is lust conceived? In your mind; that is where the root begins. Christ shows exactly how: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” That is how lust is conceived.

We are living in an evil world, and we all see beautiful women. A picture of an immodestly dressed woman was put on the screen and the brothers were asked one by one what they saw. One liked the way she dressed. Another said she is beautiful, but the way she dresses you have to hate that thing, she has to be modest. Another said, I have been in the world a lot longer than in the truth, so I am working on hating it. What you see on the screen you see every damn day when you go outside, and some of you break your neck walking down the street.

You have to train yourself to hate evil. It doesn’t come naturally; you cannot come to the truth and all of a sudden hate what you see out there. When you see her, train your mind: she has AIDS, she stinks, she has to be a man. If you don’t, you will always be watching and desiring these things. Older brothers with experience have matured past it; the young brothers dealing with youthful lusts have to train. Sisters, before the truth many of you walked around in miniskirts and spandex, giggling and giving out your number to every dude on the block, and now you have changed how you dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up.

So you see it, and in your mind you say, damn, I don’t mind sleeping with that. When you allow that thought, lust is conceived, and sin comes forth. But if the thought comes and you shake it off, what’s wrong with you, God is going to kill you, stop thinking like that, it is not conceived. If you sit down and entertain it, it brings forth sin. That is why Christ says adultery doesn’t start when you literally lie down with a woman; it starts in your mind. “and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Some say I fornicated and I didn’t die; that death is damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you.

precepts.text: Let your communication be yea, yea; nay, nay: whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. Lying to your brothers is evil, and evil is condemned by the Lord, who rewards every man according to his deeds.
precepts.point: If the Lord exposes you through people volunteering your business unasked, he wants you to get right before you do it to the wrong person and the brothers find out at your funeral. You can hate the messenger or recognize the mercy, apologize, make amends, and walk in the spirit.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.” When you say yes, I am going to do it, do it. When you say no, you can’t, then don’t. But never say yes, get paid to do the job, and then not do it. Christ put it this way: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

You are evil when you lie to your brothers. Anything other than yea and nay is evil, and if you are evil you are going to be condemned: not by us, but by the Lord. Condemn means to declare reprehensible, wrong or evil, usually after weighing evidence. The Lord is going to review your case like a court docket: the state versus so-and-so, how do you plead, not guilty, bring the witness. He didn’t know they had the witnesses.

The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good, and he rewards every man according to his deeds. Curse not the king in your chamber, lest a bird carry the news. You do evil in a different state with somebody we never met, and another brother goes to that state for a job and meets the same person. After a joyful Sabbath together, two brothers got in the car, one pocket-dialed the captain, and he heard them talking trash about all the ranking men. When questioned, the first thing was a lie.

When people bring up your evil without anybody asking one question, the Lord is exposing you because he wants you to get right. He could have let you do it to the wrong person, and we find out at your funeral: he stole a hundred grand and a dude put two in his back. You can sit home and hate the messenger, or recognize the mistake, apologize, make amends and walk in the spirit so blessing comes your way. The choice is yours.

precepts.text: Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof.
precepts.point: Ye are the light of the world; a city set on a hill cannot be hid. Keeping the commandments makes Israel stand out, and when they ask where you are from, don't hide it.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
Where does the light of Matthew 5 come from? Baruch says: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” That is the end if you reject it.

“Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it”: take hold of the book of the commandments. “Walk in the presence of the light thereof”: the light is the commandments in the book. Walk in them, “that thou mayest be illuminated.” Enlightened. You become a light in a dark place, the light that cannot be hid.

That is why “A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.” Come to this truth and start applying the laws of God and the commandments, and you cannot hide. You dress different, act different, walk different, talk different. How was your Christmas? I don't celebrate that. How was your New Year? I took a nap; a regular day. Thanksgiving, birthdays, the same. And they keep prying: where you from? Who learned you? Esau asks it, Ishmael asks it, Moab asks it, because they see something different in you, that spark, that light.

So don't hide it. “Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel”; you came to this truth to bring forth the wisdom and the light, giving light to the house of our people Israel. “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works”, so our people may see it and maybe take that light themselves and repent.

precepts.text: Show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded.
precepts.point: The gifts under the tree are offerings at the heathen altar.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
The heathen offered their sacrifices under every green tree and under every thick oak, where they offered sweet savour to their idols. Matthew 5 shows what a sacrifice is called: “if thou bring thy gift to the altar”, and “Leave there thy gift before the altar”, and “then come and offer thy gift”. The gift is the sacrifice.

Matthew 8 proves it again. Christ healed the leper and told him: “See thou tell no man; but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.” Moses commanded a gift, a sacrifice. The offering at the altar is called a gift.

So when the heathen sacrifice under a tree, they put gifts under the tree. You do not put gifts on top of the tree, beside the tree, or hang them on the tree. You put them under the tree. Where did you learn that from? The gifts under the Christmas tree are offerings at the heathen altar.

Isaiah 57 shows what else was under the tree: “Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children”. Those children were gifts too, slain under the tree. That is why they use the children to allure us in all the most popular holidays, Halloween and Christmas.

precepts.text: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise.
precepts.point: The gifts under the tree are offerings at the heathen altar.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
“Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise”. Why? Because you have technology. You have Google. You can easily look this up and see it is pagan. But because we are so covetous and want that self-gratification, the gifts blind us: Thanksgiving gifts, Valentine's Day gifts, New Year's gifts, Halloween gifts, Christmas gifts, the Easter suit, your Sunday finest on Easter. Always gifts.

“And stop up his mouth that he cannot reprove.” He knows it is wrong. He knows it is evil. But he will not say anything, and he will even fight for it. Many black and brown men will battle for Christmas for hours; ask one if he is married and he says yes. So you are scared to lose a vagina. Tell your wife today, babe, Christmas is pagan, we are not celebrating it no more, and she will put a lock and key on that box, and you will never see it again. The woman has got you by the balls, gift wrapped under the tree. That is the ordinance.

So the gifts under the tree are not harmless. They are the offering at the heathen altar, and they blind the eyes of the wise and stop the mouth of the man who should reprove it.

precepts.text: Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets; not one jot or one tittle shall pass from the law.
precepts.point: The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed”: life for life. This law is given to Noah, way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses.

The laws were never done away with. Christ says “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.” Not one jot or tittle passes from the law, and that includes the law of life for life given here.

precepts.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God; Abram was a peacemaker.
precepts.point: Be solution minded and fix problems using the scriptures; blessed are the peacemakers.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
“Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.” Abram was a peacemaker. When the herdmen strove, he said, “Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren.”

That was the spirit of Abram: he would de-escalate and look for solutions. “Is not the whole land before thee?” If you go left I go right; if you go right I go left. You cannot argue with that.

Be solution minded and fix problems using the scriptures. The peacemaker is called a child of God, and Abram showed how it is done: not by winning the argument, but by ending the strife between brethren.

precepts.text: Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil; not one jot or tittle passes from the law till all be fulfilled.
precepts.point: If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

note.label: Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution

precepts.why:
“Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.”

The law of restitution did not pass. We are in a different situation, where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback, five for an ox and four for a sheep. Do not be stealing.

precepts.text: Love your enemies: read with Exodus 23:4-5 and Deuteronomy 22:1-4, the enemy to be loved and helped is the brother of thine own nation that hates thee.
precepts.point: Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep Deuteronomy 22:1-4 and Leviticus 19:17-18 in your hip pocket with this verse.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you”.

Matthew 5:44 is misconstrued to mean the other nations. Read it with Exodus 23:4-5 and Deuteronomy 22:1-4: the enemy to be loved, the one that hates you whom you do good to, is the brother of thine own nation that hates thee. Bringing back his ox and helping with his ass is doing good to them that hate you.

precepts.text: Love your enemies speaks of your brother you are at odds with, not the nations Israel was sold under.
precepts.point: If Israel obeyed the angel's voice, the Lord would be an enemy unto their enemies and cut off the nations of the land before them. The scripture makes a distinction: the enemy whose ox or ass you must bring back and help is your brother that hates you, as the parallel law shows by using the word brother; the enemies of the nations are those the Most High said He would cut off. So love thine enemies does not mean the nation Israel was sold to; it speaks of your brother that you may be at odds with.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you”.

Love thine enemies does not mean the nation Israel was sold to. The law that says bring back thine enemy's ox and help him that hateth thee is the law that says thy brother's ass or his ox; the enemy is your brother that you may be at odds with. The enemies of the nations are those the Most High said He would cut off when Israel obeyed the Angel's voice, and He would be an enemy unto those enemies.

precepts.text: Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
precepts.point: A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for better is it that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. Christ set the same standard on the mouth: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
Christ set the same standard on the mouth: “let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

Pronouncing with the lips to do evil or to do good with an oath is the more than these. Better not to swear at all than to be guilty in one of these and need a lamb or a kid of the goats for atonement.

precepts.text: Swear not at all; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay, for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
precepts.point: Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

note.label: Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy

precepts.why:
Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High; that is swearing by His name falsely. Christ took it further: “ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: But I say unto you, Swear not at all.”

Not by heaven, “for it is God’s throne”; not by the earth, “for it is his footstool”; not by Jerusalem; and “Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.” Do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

“But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him. In your repentance take swearing out of your speech.

precepts.text: Ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye; but I say unto you that ye resist not evil; Christ magnified the law for how brothers deal with brothers.
precepts.point: Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience, and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that.

note.label: Leviticus 24: The Pure Oil, the Shewbread, and the Blasphemer

precepts.why:
“Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: as he hath caused a blemish in a man, so shall it be done to him again.” When Christ came he taught the proper understanding of eye for eye for dealing inside the nation: “Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil.”

As the Son of God he had authority to magnify the law: “whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also. And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.”

Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that here.

precepts.text: Perform unto the Lord thine oaths; but swear not at all, and let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.
precepts.point: Christ taught on this because a vow is dangerous: you must pay your vow. Better not to swear at all, but let your communication be yea, yea; that is why we just say Lord's will, Lord's will I get this done.

note.label: Leviticus 27: Vows and Estimations

precepts.why:
Christ taught on this because a vow is dangerous: you must pay your vow. He said, “ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths”.

“But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.”

Better not to swear at all: “let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” That is why we just say Lord’s will, Lord’s will I get this done.

precepts.text: Swear not at all; let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
precepts.point: Swearing on the Bible in the court system is another matter: be subject unto the higher powers, for the powers that be are ordained of God, and you also have the option to affirm; either way, tell the truth.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
Christ took the law of vows further. “Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King.”

“Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” Under Christ we do not swear at all.

That is why we say the Lord’s will: the Lord’s will I will be there, the Lord’s will I will teach that day. Yea, yea and nay, nay, and nothing bound on the soul that the flesh may not perform.

precepts.text: Ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye; but Christ says resist not evil, meaning do not seek revenge, not that you allow yourself to be beaten down.
precepts.point: Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

precepts.why:
In this time under Moses it was “life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.” If a man knocked out your tooth, the recompense was exact, and it went through the judges one way or another; thus saith the law.

Christ spoke on this saying: “Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.” He spoke on it because exact retaliation between men creates a never-ending cycle of vengeance and hatred.

Resist not evil means do not seek revenge. Turning the other cheek does not mean letting somebody beat you down into the dirt; it means when somebody does something to you, do not come back later seeking revenge.

precepts.text: That is why Christ went on to say, Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay. Whatever comes out of your mouth, be upright and honest, and do that which comes out of thy mouth.
precepts.point: She said to Eli, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the Lord. For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. That is great faith right there that Hannah had, and she kept her promise: Hannah was an upright and honest woman.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
That is why Christ went on to say, “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

Whatever comes out of your mouth, be upright and honest, and do that which comes out of thy mouth. Hannah said she would give the child to the Lord all the days of his life, and she did: “as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord.” Her yea was yea.

precepts.text: Whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment, the same judgment as a murderer; anger without a cause is counted as murder in the spirit.
precepts.point: And Saul eyed David from that day and forward. What was behind that eye? Envy. The envious man is not satisfied with his own portion; Saul had his thousands and still had the kingdom, but his eye was on David's portion, and iniquity dried up his soul from that point forward.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

precepts.why:
Christ took the law, “Thou shalt not kill”, and went into the spirit of it: “whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment.” That is the same judgment as a murderer. Anger without a cause is counted as murder in the spirit.

That is where Saul was. David had caused him nothing, yet Saul “was very wroth”, and the wrath had somewhere to go: “Saul eyed David from that day and forward.”

precepts.text: Love your enemies; Saul was David's enemy, but David loved him, and that is the understanding Christ was going into.
precepts.point: Note Saul's words: why hast thou sent away mine enemy? Saul and David were brothers, both Israel, Benjamin and Judah; Saul made his brother his enemy, and David loved him anyway. That is the understanding of Christ's words on loving your enemy: David exemplified it with Saul.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.”

Note Saul's words: “Why hast thou deceived me so, and sent away mine enemy, that he is escaped?” Saul and David were brothers, both Israel, Benjamin and Judah. Saul made his brother his enemy, and David loved him anyway. That is the understanding Christ was going into: David exemplified it with Saul.

precepts.text: Christ simplified it: let your communication be yea, yea, nay, nay, for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
precepts.point: The lesson the Most High is teaching Israel here is to pay what you vow. Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay; Saul went back on his word after he had given his yea to the Amorites, and the whole house paid for it.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

precepts.why:
“But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” Christ simplified it.

Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay. Saul went back on his word after he had given his yea to the Amorites, and the Lord sent three years of famine for it, until seven of Saul’s sons were given up to be hanged unto the Lord. The lesson the Most High is teaching Israel here is to pay what you vow.

precepts.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven; the same thing, the poor are the Israelites.
precepts.point: Blessed is he that considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble. This applies to the whole nation, because we are the poor.

note.label: Psalm 41: Blessed Is He That Considers the Poor

precepts.why:
“Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” The same thing: the poor are the Israelites, and the kingdom is theirs. Isaiah says the poor of his people trust in Zion, and Christ says the poor in spirit have the kingdom of heaven.

So “Blessed is he that considereth the poor” is about considering the Israelites, the whole nation. The Lord will deliver him in time of trouble and strengthen him “upon the bed of languishing”; and like David, he says “Lord, be merciful unto me: heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee.”

precepts.text: Ye are the salt of the earth, and if the salt loses its savor it is good for nothing but to be cast out and trodden under foot; ye are the light of the world, a city set on a hill that cannot be hid.
precepts.point: The kings assembled, saw Zion, marveled, were troubled and hasted away; fear and pain took hold of them as of a woman in travail.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
Israel is the joy of the earth, the salt of the earth: “Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.”

You cannot make America great without the slaves, the strongest people on earth working for crumbs; that is the salt. Israel's savour is the commandments. Having lost the identity and the commandments, Israel became good for nothing but to be trodden under foot, only worth more when keeping the commandments and knowing the identity. Then Israel is the light of the world, the city set on a hill that cannot be hid, the city the kings saw and marvelled at.

precepts.text: Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill the animal sacrifice.
precepts.point: Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil the animal sacrifice.

So the law and the prophets still stand, and they agree. When the psalm says he gave Israel into the hand of the heathen, “and they that hated them ruled over them”, that is the law (Leviticus 26, Deuteronomy 28) and the prophets speaking with one voice. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing.

precepts.text: The poor in spirit are blessed, and it is they whom the Most High sets on high from affliction.
precepts.point: Whoso is wise and will observe these things, even they shall understand the lovingkindness of the Lord. If you have wisdom you will observe these things.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Yet setteth he the poor on high from affliction, and maketh him families like a flock.” The poor here are the poor in spirit. “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”

The poor in spirit are blessed, and it is they whom the Most High sets on high from affliction. The righteous, those keeping God's commandments, shall see it and rejoice, and all iniquity shall stop her mouth.

precepts.text: Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law till all be fulfilled, which is a future prophecy of all coming into perfection.
precepts.point: I am Thine, save me, for I have sought Thy precepts. The wicked have waited for me to destroy me, but I will consider Thy testimonies. I have seen an end of all perfection, but Thy commandment is exceeding broad.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“For ever, O Lord, thy word is settled in heaven.” Christ says the same: “Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.”

This word has been here from the beginning and endures for ever; not one jot or tittle passes from the law until heaven and earth pass. “till all be fulfilled” is a future prophecy of all coming into perfection, which is why the psalm says “I have seen an end of all perfection: but thy commandment is exceeding broad.”

precepts.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: His rulership, his throne, will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever. He is the Most High our God and none else, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “I will abundantly bless her provision: I will satisfy her poor with bread.” Her poor are the poor in spirit, the Israelites: “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” He satisfies them with bread and the kingdom is theirs.

precepts.text: Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them that despitefully use and persecute you.
precepts.point: David showed this with Saul: he cut off the skirt of Saul's robe in the cave but would not kill the Most High's anointed, and Saul confessed David was more righteous, rewarding good for evil. The coals of fire are the shame that comes on such an enemy.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

precepts.why:
“If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink”. Christ says the same: “Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you”.

Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them that use you and persecute you. Bread and water for the hungry and thirsty enemy is doing good to them that hate you.

This concerns the enemies among your people, not the other nations. Prayers for vengeance in Luke 18 and Psalm 149 are for our natural enemies; the enemy you feed, bless and pray for is one of your own.

precepts.text: Christ's command to swear not at all, by heaven, earth, or your head, which Solomon's warning about vows supports.
precepts.point: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the angel that it was an error, lest the Most High be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands. This is what Christ meant by not swearing by heaven, earth, or your own head.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.”

This is what Christ meant by not swearing by heaven, earth or your own head, and Solomon's warning about vows supports it: “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools”, and “Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.” Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the angel that it was an error, lest the Most High be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands. Better not to swear at all; but fear the Most High.

precepts.text: Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil it, yet they twist "fulfil" to mean He abolished it.
precepts.point: With stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people; off the slave ships Israel spoke different languages, and because they did not keep the law the oppressor's culture was beaten into them until they came to understand. This Bible is the rest and the refreshing, yet they would not hear, so the word came precept upon precept that they might fall backward and be broken and snared.

note.label: Isaiah 28: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim and Precept Upon Precept
